fact: The 'little she-goat' of the charioteer — a golden point that is secretly four stars.
bio: Capella (Alpha Aurigae) is the brightest star in Auriga and the sixth-brightest in the sky, about 43 light-years away. Though it looks like one yellow star resembling the Sun, it is really two giant G-type stars orbiting closely, accompanied by a pair of faint red dwarfs.
cultural: Its Latin name means 'little she-goat' — the goat carried on the shoulder of Auriga the Charioteer, with the nearby 'Kids' at her side. As one of the northernmost bright stars, it was a familiar winter-evening marker across Europe and the Near East.
